text.p: Hsing-Hsing, the U.S. National Zoo's giant panda, underwent successful cancer surgery Tuesday and is expected to resume his normal activities within a few days, zoo officials said.
The 26-year-old panda, one of a pair given to the United States in 1972 by China following a trip there by then President Richard Nixon, was suffering from testicular cancer.

Bob Hoage, the Zoo spokesman, said a team of three veterinarians successfully removed the tumourous testicle and took out the other as a precautionary measure. They also removed a nearby lymph node to check for any abnormalities.

Hsing-Hsing has never produced an heir and was enduring his fifth breeding season without a female after the death of his mate, Ling-Ling, in 1992. At 26 he is very old for a panda, and also has arthritis.
"The Zoo's veterinarians report that the giant panda ....tolerated anaesthesia and the surgery without complication and was returned to his home at the panda house," Hoage said.
The operation lasted about an hour and, while at the Zoo's veterinary hospital, Hsing-Hsing's teeth were cleaned and radiographs taken.

"National Zoo pathologist Richard Montali will evaluate the tissues that were removed from Hsing-Hsing and, when this analysis is completed, veterinarians will have a better idea of the animal's prognosis," Hoage said.
The pandas have been the star attraction at the zoo, drawing an estimated 75 million people to the exhibit in the past 25 years.
